source.version: arXiv 2502.11266v2 dated 24 Aug 2026 (stamp on p. 1), the author's version of the Nature Human Behaviour article doi 10.1038/s41562-026-02550-0 (footnote p. 2), with the Supplementary Information appended (PDF pp. 53-73, numbered S1 onward). Read from the PDF on file; numbers checked against PDF pages.
source.title_on_document: The Shrinking Landscape of Linguistic Diversity in the Age of Large Language Models

supplement.where: Supplementary Information appended to the arXiv PDF, pp. 53-73 (S1 onward); code at https://github.com/zhpinkman/LLMs-effect-on-linguistic-diversity, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21633457 (Code availability, p. 38)
supplement.holds: Appendix A semantic-similarity tests; Appendix B Levene results for all rewriting prompts and the Study 2 datasets (Tables B4-B6); Appendix C lexical shifts (Table C7); Appendix D trait-prediction details; Appendix F exact correlation coefficients for Study 3

paper_design_summary: No people were assigned to AI assistance; the analyses use existing corpora (p. 23, Methods). Study 1a relates the monthly average of five feature-specific writing-complexity variances in Reddit stories, Patch news, and arXiv abstracts to ChatGPT's launch and detected AI-written shares; Study 1b compares variance of a per-document average complexity score before and after automated rewriting of 1,000 pre-ChatGPT texts each from Reddit and arXiv by GPT-3.5, Llama 3 70B, and Gemini Pro (pp. 24-31, Methods 1.1-1.7). Study 2 examines author-trait prediction, while Study 3 compares lexical cue-trait associations and across-text variance of lexical-category frequencies in original and rewritten texts (pp. 31-36, Methods 1.8-1.10; p. 68, Table C7).

studies.label: Study 1a (observational trends in Reddit, Patch News, arXiv)

assignment.quote: This work did not involve the collection of new data from human participants.

participants.who: Corpus of public texts: Reddit r/WritingPrompts stories (N = 318,490, Jan 2018 to Nov 2024), Patch.com local news articles (N = 379,583 by 19,584 contributors, Jan 2018 to Nov 2023), arXiv cs.CL and cs.CV abstracts (N = 80,238 papers, 161,265 authors, Jan 2018 to Nov 2024). Analyzed as monthly series: arXiv 83, Reddit 83, Patch News 71 months.
participants.country: United States (Patch); not stated for Reddit and arXiv
participants.quote: Sample sizes for the underlying texts are: arXiv N = 80,238 papers, Patch News N = 379,583 articles, Reddit N = 318,490 stories.

ai_tool.name_model: Any LLM (ChatGPT launch as the event); AI use detected with Binoculars
ai_tool.how_used: Not observed; the monthly share of texts that Binoculars classifies as AI-written proxies adoption.

task.description: Naturally occurring writing: creative stories (Reddit), local news, scientific abstracts.

outcomes.name: Monthly average of feature-specific writing-complexity variances: shift at ChatGPT launch (discontinuous growth model)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Monthly variance of each of five complexity features (Simpson index, Shannon entropy, average dependency link length, type-token ratio, hapax legomena), averaged into one composite; DGM by GLS with AR(1) errors; Time, ONSET (level shift), POST (slope change). Per-feature trends in Extended Data Fig. 5 (p. 27).

diversity_detail.metric: Monthly average of the five feature-specific variances across texts within each corpus (Methods 1.3, pp. 25-26)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All texts posted in each month, per corpus
diversity_detail.uncertainty: GLS with AR(1) errors on the monthly variance series; asymptotic Wald tests
diversity_detail.notes: Lower variance = less diversity; negative changes indicate homogenization. The metric follows Methods 1.3 (pp. 25-26), which averages feature-specific monthly variances. Figure 1 (p. 6) instead calls it the monthly variance of an aggregate score; the unresolved wording discrepancy is recorded in open_questions. Study 1b explicitly uses variance of a per-document average (p. 31, Methods 1.7).

outcomes.name: Monthly AI-written rate predicting writing-complexity variance (Granger and GAM tests)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Same monthly average of feature-specific variances as S1-O1 (pp. 25-26, Methods 1.3); bivariate VAR Granger F-test with AIC-selected lag, plus a GAM-based nonlinear test.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Higher monthly share of texts flagged as AI-written
contrasts.control_arm: Lower monthly share of texts flagged as AI-written
contrasts.reported: Granger: arXiv lag 5, F(5,66) = 2.55, p = .036; Reddit lag 20, F(20,21) = 3.75, p = .002; Patch News lag 20, F(20,8) = 2.30, p = .114. GAM: arXiv F = 2.45, edf = 7.4, p = .026; Reddit F = 5.11, edf = 5.1, p < .001; Patch News F = 1.82, edf = 3.5, p = .151.

diversity_detail.metric: Monthly average of the five feature-specific variances across texts within each corpus (Methods 1.3, pp. 25-26)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All texts posted in each month, per corpus
diversity_detail.uncertainty: F-tests on VAR coefficients and on GAM smooth terms
diversity_detail.notes: Tests are not signed; the text (pp. 7-8) reads the arXiv and Reddit results as AI usage predicting reductions in variance. Patch News not significant.

studies.label: Study 1b (LLM rewrites of pre-ChatGPT Reddit and arXiv texts)

participants.who: Corpus: 1,000 randomly selected human-authored Reddit posts and 1,000 arXiv abstracts published before ChatGPT's release, each rewritten by three LLMs under neutral prompts. No people involved.
participants.quote: From each source, we randomly select 1,000 human-authored texts published before the release of ChatGPT

ai_tool.how_used: The authors prompt each model to rewrite the human text (main text: Rephrase and Syntax Grammar prompts; 12 prompts in all, Section 1.5, p. 29); no human in the loop.

task.description: Polishing or rephrasing existing human texts (creative stories and scientific abstracts).

outcomes.name: Variance of writing-complexity score, original vs LLM-rewritten texts
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Variance across texts of the per-text composite complexity score (five features as in Study 1a); median-centered Levene's test; bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples) on the variance ratio orig/LLM. All 12 prompts and the Study 2 datasets in Appendix B, Tables B4-B6 (pp. 55-58).

contrasts.treatment_arm: LLM-rewritten texts (GPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemini; Rephrase and Syntax Grammar prompts)
contrasts.reported: arXiv original variance 0.0090, Reddit 0.0091. arXiv after rewriting: Gemini R 0.0071 (F = 5.062, p = .024), SG 0.0074 (p = .034); GPT3.5 R 0.0070 (p = .025), SG 0.0071 (p = .012); Llama 3 R 0.0064 (F = 12.007, p < .001), SG 0.0111 (F = 3.377, p = .066, 95% CI [0.59, 0.85]). Reddit: Gemini R 0.0076 (p = .145), SG 0.0069 (p = .020); GPT3.5 R 0.0063 (p = .014), SG 0.0068 (p = .017); Llama 3 R 0.0045 (F = 19.387, p < .001, 95% CI [1.29, 2.33]), SG 0.0069 (p = .047). Abstract: 'reducing writing-complexity variance by a statistically significant 21–50% across datasets and models (p ≤ .05)'. 11 of 12 printed cells lower; Llama 3 SG on arXiv higher.

diversity_detail.metric: Variance across texts of the composite writing-complexity score
diversity_detail.computed_over: All 1,000 texts per source, original set vs rewritten set for each LLM x prompt
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Levene's test (median-centered) and nonparametric bootstrap CI on the variance ratio
diversity_detail.notes: Rewrites are paired with their originals; semantic similarity stays high (87% of cosine similarities above 0.95, p. 8).

studies.label: Study 2 (predicting author traits from original vs LLM-rewritten texts)

participants.who: Existing corpora pairing writing with independently measured author traits: Essays contains 2,348 essays, each from a unique author (personality); Congress has a final sample of 710 speakers, with their longest utterances assembled toward a target of 4,000 words per speaker (age, gender, party); Empathic Conversations contains 711 reaction essays from 57 authors, concatenated by author (empathy). Methods 1.8 reports YourMorals as 107,798 Facebook posts from 2,691 users, concatenated by author (moral values), while Extended Data Figure 1 reports n = 3,641 for that dataset. The YourMorals analysis count is unresolved. These are source-text and source-author counts, not people assigned to AI assistance; n_randomized and n_analyzed remain null. The texts were rewritten by the same three LLMs as Study 1b.
participants.quote: the dataset comprises 711 essays written by 57 authors, each contributing between 1 and 72 reaction essays.
participants.locator: pp. 31-33, Methods 1.8 (Congress and Essays, p. 32; Empathic Conversations and YourMorals, p. 33); p. 9, Extended Data Figure 1 caption

ai_tool.how_used: Authors' LLM rewrites of each text; classifiers trained on original texts are applied to the rewritten texts.

task.description: Polishing or rephrasing personal essays, social-media posts, reflections, and floor speeches.

outcomes.name: Classifier F1 for predicting author traits, original vs LLM-rewritten texts
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Mean macro-F1 of trait classifiers (TF-IDF or OpenAI embeddings with several classifier families, plus Longformer) evaluated on original test sets and their rewritten counterparts. Two-sided paired t-tests compare classifier-evaluation runs across configurations, cross-validation folds, and random seeds, not pairs of individual outputs. Methods 1.9 (pp. 33-34) specifies 5-fold cross-validation and 40 repetitions with different seeds, retaining above-random models with at least 20 successful runs. Table D9 (p. 69, S17) reports N as paired observations (e.g., age N = 805); there is no single common n_units for the combined trait outcome, so n_units remains null. This measures retained author-trait signal, not creativity or diversity.

contrasts.reported: Mean F1 OG vs LLM: Age group .351 vs .260 (diff .091, 95% CI [.079, .102], t = 15.397, df 804, d = 0.543); Empathy .657 vs .603 (d = 0.397); Personality .658 vs .602 (d = 0.343); Gender .694 vs .623 (d = 0.431); Morality .640 vs .578 (d = 0.355); Affiliation .664 vs .591 (d = 0.433); all p < .001. Text: 'an average 6% decline in predictive accuracy (absolute F1 score)'.

studies.label: Study 3 (lexical cue-trait associations and lexical-category diversity in original vs LLM-rewritten texts)

participants.who: Uses the same corpora as Study 2 (p. 18). Existing corpora pairing writing with independently measured author traits: Essays contains 2,348 essays, each from a unique author (personality); Congress has a final sample of 710 speakers, with their longest utterances assembled toward a target of 4,000 words per speaker (age, gender, party); Empathic Conversations contains 711 reaction essays from 57 authors, concatenated by author (empathy). Methods 1.8 reports YourMorals as 107,798 Facebook posts from 2,691 users, concatenated by author (moral values), while Extended Data Figure 1 reports n = 3,641 for that dataset. The YourMorals analysis count is unresolved. These are source-text and source-author counts, not people assigned to AI assistance; n_randomized and n_analyzed remain null.
participants.quote: Using the same corpora from Study 2, which pair texts with independently collected author personal traits
participants.locator: p. 18, Study 3; pp. 31-33, Methods 1.8; p. 9, Extended Data Figure 1 caption

ai_tool.how_used: Authors' automated LLM rewrites, as in Study 2; the lexical-category variance comparisons in Extended Data Figure 6 and Table C7 use GPT-3.5 with the Rephrase prompt (p. 36). Cue-trait associations are also compared across LLMs and prompts (Appendix F).

task.description: Compares lexical cue-trait associations and the across-text variance of lexical-category relative frequencies between existing human texts and automated LLM rewrites.

outcomes.name: Across-text variance of lexical-category relative frequencies, original vs LLM-rewritten texts
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Per-text frequencies of lexical categories (category word count relative to total word count), min-max scaled to [0, 1], compared between original texts and GPT-3.5 Rephrase rewrites. Extended Data Figure 6 (p. 36) displays the distributions; Table C7 (p. 68, S16) gives category-specific sample sizes, original/rewritten variances, and Levene tests. The outcome family includes pronouns, affect, emotion words, swear words, social and death-related words, conversational markers, assent, nonfluencies, and fillers across Essays, Empathic Conversations, Congress, and YourMorals. Appendix C (pp. 57-58, S5-S6) discusses similar patterns across models and prompts.

contrasts.reported: Table C7 examples, original / rewritten variances with category-specific n and Levene F and p: Essays pronoun, n = 2,037, 0.0465 / 0.0383, F = 12.704, p < .001; Empathic Conversations pronoun, n = 49, 0.0368 / 0.0257, F = 2.469, p = 0.119; Congress pronoun, n = 623, 0.0440 / 0.0162, F = 159.979, p < .001; YourMorals pronoun, n = 3,203, 0.0442 / 0.0155, F = 472.608, p < .001. Direction varies by category: Essays emo_sad, n = 996, increases from 0.0539 to 0.0589, F = 4.189, p = 0.041. These are text-distribution counts as labeled in Table C7, not counts of people receiving AI assistance; no single n_units applies to the combined outcome.
contrasts.locator: p. 68 (S16), Table C7, pronoun rows for all four datasets and Essays emo_sad row; p. 36, Extended Data Figure 6

diversity_detail.metric: Across-text variance of each lexical category's relative frequency after min-max scaling to [0, 1]
diversity_detail.computed_over: Original texts and their GPT-3.5 Rephrase rewrites, separately within each lexical category and corpus (Essays, Empathic Conversations, Congress, YourMorals)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Levene's tests of equality of variances; category-specific F statistics and p values in Table C7 (p. 68, S16)
diversity_detail.notes: Original and rewritten versions are paired by text. Lower variance indicates greater homogenization; directions and significance vary by category. n_units is null because Table C7 reports different n values by category and dataset. The common-per-dataset counts claimed in Extended Data Figure 6 conflict with Table C7; see open_questions.

eligibility.reason: No people were randomly assigned to AI assistance, and there is no human AI-assistance sample meeting the people-count criterion; the paper analyzes existing corpora (p. 23, Methods; pp. 29-31, Methods 1.5-1.7). Study 1a compares temporal corpus trends with output-scored diversity outcomes, supporting paper-level observational context (pp. 6-7, Figure 1 and Tables 1-2). Study 1b compares automated LLM rewrites with original human texts. Study 2 is model-only trait prediction. Study 3 compares lexical cue-trait associations and also contains AI-versus-human diversity comparisons of lexical-category variances (pp. 35-36, Methods 1.10 and Extended Data Figure 6; p. 68, Table C7).

one_line_finding: Post-launch changes in the slope of the monthly average of feature-specific complexity variances were negative for Reddit (beta = -0.0021, p < .001), Patch News (-0.0022, p = .049), and arXiv (-0.0014, p < .001; Table 1, p. 7), while LLM rewrites lowered variance of per-text average complexity in 11 of 12 Table 3 cells (e.g., Reddit 0.0091 to 0.0045 with Llama 3 Rephrase, p. 11), which the abstract summarizes as a 21-50% reduction (p. 2).
open_questions: Unresolved YourMorals count: Methods 1.8 (p. 33) reports 107,798 Facebook posts from 2,691 users, concatenated by author, but Extended Data Figure 1 (p. 9) reports n = 3,641. The document does not reconcile these counts; no reconciled analysis count is inferred, and the participants.n_analyzed fields remain null.

Unresolved Study 1a metric definition: Methods 1.3 (pp. 25-26) computes each feature's monthly variance and then averages those variances, whereas Figure 1 (p. 6) calls the outcome the monthly variance of an aggregate writing-complexity score. This form follows the methods definition. Study 1b explicitly computes variance of a per-document average (p. 31, Methods 1.7); the two operations cannot be assumed identical.

Unresolved lexical-category sample sizes: Extended Data Figure 6 (p. 36) says all categories share the same n within each dataset (Essays 2,348; Empathic Conversations 711; Congress 710; YourMorals 3,641), but Table C7 (p. 68, S16) reports category-specific n (e.g., Essays pronoun 2,037 vs emo_sad 996; Empathic Conversations pronoun 49). Table C7 values are retained with their labels; no common analysis n is inferred.

Unresolved GPT3.5 Syntax Grammar / Reddit test statistics: Table 3 (p. 11) reports F = 5.652, p = .017, while Table B5 (p. 57, S5) reports F = 6.652, p = .018 for the same displayed variance change, 0.0091 to 0.0068. The contrast retains the main-table values; the PDF provides no reconciliation.

Unresolved standardized effects: Table 4 (p. 14) reports Cohen's d = 0.543 for age, 0.431 for gender, and 0.433 for affiliation; Table D9 (p. 69, S17) reports 0.776, 0.603, and 0.610, respectively, with the same corresponding means, t statistics, and degrees of freedom. The PDF does not reconcile the values or explain a different standardizer. S3-O1 retains the cited main-table values.

applied.old: In Reddit stories, Patch news, and arXiv abstracts, the monthly variance of writing complexity fell after ChatGPT's launch (POST slopes -0.0014, -0.0022, -0.0021, all p < .05; Table 1, p. 7), and LLM rewrites of 1,000 pre-ChatGPT texts per source cut that variance in 11 of 12 model-prompt cells (e.g. Reddit 0.0091 to 0.0045 with Llama 3; Table 3, p. 11), which the abstract summarizes as a 21-50% reduction (p. 2).
applied.new: Post-launch changes in the slope of the monthly average of feature-specific complexity variances were negative for Reddit (beta = -0.0021, p < .001), Patch News (-0.0022, p = .049), and arXiv (-0.0014, p < .001; Table 1, p. 7), while LLM rewrites lowered variance of per-text average complexity in 11 of 12 Table 3 cells (e.g., Reddit 0.0091 to 0.0045 with Llama 3 Rephrase, p. 11), which the abstract summarizes as a 21-50% reduction (p. 2).
applied.locator: p. 7, Table 1 caption and POST rows; p. 11, Table 3; p. 2, Abstract
